- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 68.83 → 74.25, 71.64 → 74.25).
- Model underreacts to recent downward trends; fails to adjust forecast mean downward when prices show clear mean reversion.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values; subtract 2–5% of forecasted value for correction if recent 7–14d mean is below 65.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >10% in first 5 days, reduce subsequent forecast by 1–3% per day to avoid overcorrection lag.
- Model exhibits “lagged response” to price drops — forecasts remain high for 3–5 days after true price declines.
- When history includes a recent sharp rise (>10% from 14d prior), forecast should be capped at +5% above prior peak to avoid overshoot.
- If forecast > 75 and true outcome < 70, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence in high-price regime.
